scope: Long plain text only after existing splitting threshold; 32 short FLORES dev rows joined with newlines per language. Same segmentation, models and precision. Shared native inference budget, no batching or kernel change.

method.httpCpuThreads: production automatic selection; paired choices retained below
method.httpWarmup: one per case plus two full rounds at each concurrency; startup excluded
method.engineWarmup: one per case plus one full round at each concurrency; startup excluded

limitations: One local Linux x64 CPU and two language directions; small synthetic documents assembled from dev rows, not production traffic.
Single-document speedup uses otherwise idle capacity of the existing inference budget; it is not a faster ONNX kernel or per-core improvement.
No stable multi-document throughput improvement is claimed; paired variation retained.

Four-document standard zh-Hans_en HTTP median block latency increased 5.12% (paired speed ratios 0.879 to 1.167); fast zh-Hans_en increased 2.57%. This is accepted only as a single-document latency improvement, not a general throughput win.
HTTP standard mode uses production autotuning; comparisons with different CPU thread counts are confounded and must be read separately.
No load above four documents, mixed arrival latency, long-duration memory test or cross-hardware test.
Nested splits stay serial; extra workers retire when another request is running and do not restart later.
Native fallback was tested by injected errors followed by actual CPU inference, not by a natural runtime crash.
No npm publication. Temporary scripts and source data remain local; this is not a portable reproduction bundle.
